overview.oneLineTake: The AI relief rally cut fear fast, but with the Fed leaning hawkish and the move driven by one stock, expect choppy follow-through rather than a clean all-clear.
themes: AI relief rally: Nvidia reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO triggered a 31% one-day jump in the stock and pulled Micron, AMD, CoreWeave and Oracle sharply higher. Wall Street posted its best day in over a year after last week's correction.
Index move is large: SPY closed at 722.29, up 4.7% from the prior close of 689.81. QQQ closed at 651.03, up 7.0% from 608.45 (Alpha Vantage, Nov 23).
Fed stays hawkish: NY Fed's Williams signaled higher rates are likely over time to address inflation, and the 2-year yield jumped. The 10-year yield was 4.92% on Nov 20.
Rotation out of defensives: consumer staples were among the S&P 500's biggest losers as money chased AI names.
Crypto lagged: Bitcoin sat out the rally amid a reported $1.8 billion ETF outflow.
risks: A one-day squeeze after a rout is not a confirmed bottom. Short covering did much of the work, and analysts still call it a bottom only for now.
Washington backlash over the Nvidia decision, and a US probe into Nvidia chip smuggling, add headline risk to the AI trade.
Rate-hike odds and spreading inflation could cap multiples if the rebound fades.
Gold has been weak and Congo halted cobalt exports, so commodity cross-currents stay noisy.

nq.summary: NDX cash ripped 6.86% to 26,746 Monday, its best session since April last year, after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang and NVDA jumped 31.5%. NQ is giving back a little overnight while Williams keeps hikes on the table, so follow through is the test. Thesis: neutral, 4/10, two way trade between squeeze strength and a hawkish Fed. Invalidation: close above 27,019. NDX levels: resistance 27,000 (round), 27,019 (Mon H), 27,500 (round); support 26,500 (round), 26,386 (Mon L), 26,000 (round).
